arms.label: Without: free-choice loop over raw tables
arms.adds: Sonnet chooses among raw ERP table queries and does the policy arithmetic itself; no step budget, no policy tool

arms.label: With: 4-step budget + policy tool (Sonnet)
arms.adds: 4-step budget and the deterministic policy tool, with one narrow query and the policy manual cached

arms.label: With: 4-step budget + policy tool (Haiku-first)
arms.adds: The same on Haiku; Sonnet takes over when the policy tool flags a multi-factor dispute

notes: Without: the free-choice loop over the five raw SELECT * tools on Sonnet (no step budget beyond a 12-turn safety cap, no policy tool, no prompt cache). With: a 4-step budget and the deterministic policy tool (run_policy_tolerance_gate; the commit is refused until it has run), and the with-design also uses one narrow query (fetch_3way_match_bundle) in place of the raw tables and sends the policy manual as a cached prefix, so the difference is not the budget and the tool alone.
The policy manual (SOP-AP-3WAY-2026.v4) is the system text of every version. The without-version runs the free-choice protocol; the with-versions run the app's rung-2 and rung-3 prompts unchanged.

Escalation (Haiku-first version): the run switches to Sonnet from the next turn when the policy tool sets escalation_required, which it does only for a multi-factor commercial dispute (two or more of: partial DOA or short receipt, signed contract amendment, unauthorized line price rise, disallowed freight; manual 6.2). Expected escalations: inv-02 and inv-12.
Thinking differs by model in the app's call function: Sonnet runs with thinking {type: between_tools}, Haiku with thinking disabled.

Each cached run starts with its own nonce line, so it writes the cache on its first turn and reads it after (cold cache per run). Costs are derived from recorded tokens with app/core/pricing.py; cold/warm by the app's _compute_step_cold_warm rule.

Loop rule: a turn cut off by max_tokens ends the run and its tool_use blocks are recorded but not executed; tool_use blocks in any other turn are executed and the loop continues, whatever the stop_reason.
Voucher ids in the without-version end in -UNB: it reuses the app session's unbounded_sonnet_loop rung id, from which the app derives the voucher-id suffix.

Tool precision (the app's metric) credits only the narrow query, the policy tool and the commit, so a raw SELECT * call is never counted optimal; it is not comparable between the without- and with-versions.
The Anthropic SDK client retries failed or timed-out calls (default max_retries=2) inside one recorded turn; a retried call is not visible in the records and may have been billed.
Limits: 12 invoices x 3 runs per version; every version committed exact vouchers on nearly every run, so the data separates the versions on cost and turns, not on accuracy.

golden_mapping.selection_rule: fixed pre-declared mapping, repeat_index 0, original invoices inv-01..03 (not selected by outcome)
